q: Laser is an acronym for Light Amplification by _____ Emission of Radiation.
e: A laser, acronym for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.

q: A laser is a source of a narrow beam of intense, monochromatic, _____ light.
e: A laser is a source of a narrow beam of intense, monochromatic, coherent light.

q: In a laser, the power supply delivers energy to the laser medium in a process called _____.
e: The power supply delivers energy to the laser medium in the form needed to excite it to emit light. This process is called pumping.

q: The optical cavity consists of two highly reflective mirrors; one is a perfect reflector and the other is a _____ reflector.
e: The other mirror with a reflectivity of about 80 to 90% (partial reflector) reflects most part of the light.

q: For stimulated emission to occur, a population _____ is needed where the upper level population is higher than the lower level.
e: For stimulated emission to occur, a population inversion would be needed.

q: Atoms undergoing stimulated emission radiate photons of the same frequency in the same direction and in _____ with the stimulating radiation.
e: Atoms undergoing stimulated emission radiate photons of the same frequency in the same direction and in phase with the stimulating radiation.

q: A typical laser beam divergence is around a _____, meaning it spreads very little over distance.
e: A typical beam divergence is around a milliradian, i.e, it will spread only to 1 m in diameter after travelling 1 km.

q: Lasers are classified into five main types, including gas lasers, solid-state lasers, and _____ lasers.
e: Lasers are classified into five main types: gas lasers, solid-state lasers, fiber lasers, liquid lasers, semiconductor lasers.

q: The laser medium can be a gas, liquid, crystalline solid or _____ crystal.
e: The laser medium (gain medium) is the material emitting the laser beam. It can be a gas, liquid, crystalline solid or semiconductor crystal.

q: One of the unique properties of a laser beam is _____, which means the light waves it contains are in phase with one another.
e: One of the unique properties of a laser beam is coherence. This means that the light waves it contains are in phase with one another.

q: In industries, high power lasers are used to cut metals and drill aerosol nozzles with required _____.
e: In industries, high power lasers are used to cut metals, drill aerosol nozzles and orifices with the required precision.

q: Lasers are used in the semiconductor industries for _____, a process used to pattern surfaces.
e: Lasers are used in the semiconductor industries for photolithography.

q: To sustain a laser action, the lower energy level must be _____ while the upper level is populated.
e: To sustain a laser action the lower level must be depopulated while the upper level is populated.

q: Laser range finders are used to determine the _____ to an object.
e: Laser range finders are used to determine the distance to an object.

q: The output power of a continuous laser beam can range from a fraction of a milliwatt to around 20 _____ in commercial lasers.
e: The power in a continuous beam can range from a fraction of a milliwatt to around 20 kilowatts in commercial lasers.
